title: E-Scooters More Dangerous than Motorbikes, Bicycles
paragraphs: E-scooters have become a popular way to get around cities. However, a new study from the UK suggests that people who ride them may suffer more serious injuries in crashes than motorcyclists or cyclists.

The study was published in the journal Scientific Reports in 2026. The researchers looked at records from a national database of people in England and Wales who were badly injured between 2020 and 2022. They also studied more than 23,000 reports of accidents involving rental e-scooters in 18 cities.

The researchers found that adults who were seriously injured while riding e-scooters were 3.5 times more likely to have a brain injury than injured motorcyclists. They were also 1.7 times more likely to have a brain injury than injured cyclists. In addition, they were more likely to have injuries to their internal organs and blood vessels. However, they were less likely to break bones.

One reason may be that few e-scooter riders wear helmets. According to reports, only about 6% of the injured e-scooter riders were wearing a helmet. This compared with about 76% of motorcyclists and 45% of cyclists.
The study also found that children made up a large share of seriously injured e-scooter riders.

However, it is important to understand what the study shows. It compared the types of injuries among people who were already in hospital. It does not mean that riding an e-scooter is three and a half times more dangerous than riding a motorcycle. This is because the researchers did not have data on how far people traveled on each type of vehicle.
The researchers support rules requiring e-scooter riders to wear helmets, as well as speed limits and safer roads.
